chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about a woman who married a man while he was married to her aunt (paternal) and her aunt (maternal). He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

And he said, 'Marry the aunt (paternal) and the aunt (maternal) to the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister, and do not marry the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister to the aunt (paternal) and the aunt (maternal) unless with their consent. And whoever does so, his marriage is invalid.'

It is possible that the two reports were issued in the manner of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because everyone who differs from us differs in this matter, and since this is its ruling, Taqiyya is permissible in it, and the report which he narrated...

key_terms.تَزَوَّجَ عَلَى: To marry (a woman) to (another woman), implying polygyny or simultaneous marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling between marrying two sisters versus marrying an aunt and her niece in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim clarifies the permissibility of polygamy among specific kinship lines, distinguishing between the absolute prohibition of marrying two sisters versus the conditional validity of marrying an aunt and niece. The text highlights the scholarly debate regarding whether these rulings reflect the actual legal status or were issued under *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) due to differing views among other schools of thought. It establishes that while marrying an aunt and niece is permissible, doing so without the mutual consent of both women renders the marriage void.
